page: Microsoft Azure E2d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL core with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 processor includes 32 KB L1D cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and includes a 77 GB local SSD.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance in single-threaded operations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1264.0 and a gzip compression speed of 24.02 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive workloads show limitations. The Stress-ng multi-core CPU score is 1840.88, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 1530.0, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is measured at 14.22 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 11.16 GB/sec for large block write operations. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also constrained, with Redis achieving 1.77 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2d_v4 offers a high memory density per vCPU for a dedicated resource class, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive multi-core processing. The inclusion of a 77 GB local SSD provides fast temporary storage. This configuration is suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, lightweight web serving, and memory-intensive single-threaded applications. It is less suited for parallel processing, heavy compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E2d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv4 family, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon 8272CL processor (1 physical core, 2 threads) with x86_64 architecture, 16.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core), and a 77 GB local SSD. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1264.0, but multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are relatively low, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1530.0 and uncached read bandwidth of 14.22 GB/sec. This server provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy, low-compute workloads. It is best suited for small databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive single-threaded tasks.
